sources.content:
# claude-toolkit

Private Claude Code plugin marketplace (`claude-toolkit`) with one plugin, `toolkit`, and a companion VS Code extension: a personal proof of concept for a project coordinator that creates and follows worker sessions. See [README.md](README.md) for setup, daily use and the board format.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | Marketplace catalogue; plugins are listed by relative `source` |
| `plugins/toolkit/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | Plugin manifest; no `version`, so each pushed commit is a release |
| `plugins/toolkit/agents/` | `coordinator` and `worker` agents; their prompts define the board protocol |
| `plugins/toolkit/hooks/` | SessionStart hook: SDD team-mailbox pull for the coordinator only |
| `vscode/` | VS Code extension, plain CommonJS with no dependencies or build: `core.js` (pure logic, tested), `extension.js` (VS Code glue) |
| `tests/` | `node --test` (unit, hook, `claude plugin validate`); `tests/coordinator.e2e.mjs` starts a real session |
| `openspec/` | OpenSpec specs and changes |

## Rules

- Compatible with SDD, separate from it: never change SDD files, rules, skills or agents, never name a skill or agent `sdd`, and use SDD only through its documented commands (the hook runs `complete-change.mjs --collab pull` and nothing else). Everything is written in English, like SDD.
- The board format lives in three places that must agree: the agent prompts, `vscode/core.js` and the README table. `tests/toolkit.test.mjs` pins the shared paths and the request shape.
- The extension starts Claude without a shell (`shellPath` plus `shellArgs`) and only with validated worker names; never build a command line from request content.
- The organization's managed policy blocks non-official marketplaces, so sessions load this clone with `--plugin-dir`: every saved file, committed or not, is live in the next session, and the extension after a VS Code reload.
- Run `node --test` before committing.
- `.gitattributes` keeps LF line endings so checkouts on Windows stay byte-identical.

# claude-toolkit

Personal Claude Code plugins, laid out as a private plugin marketplace. A proof of concept: it is compatible with the team-shared SDD skill but entirely separate from it, and never changes it. Every toolkit agent carries the `toolkit:` prefix.

## What it does

Open a project in VS Code and a **coordinator** Claude session starts in an editor tab. It reports the SDD team recap, reads the project board and asks what is next. You tell it the goal; it creates the **worker** sessions the job needs, each in its own named tab with a written brief, and follows them through SendMessage. Workers that still have open work reopen with their conversation the next time you open the project. You can still type in any worker's tab.

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| `toolkit:coordinator` and `toolkit:worker` agents | `plugins/toolkit/agents/` |
| Start-up hook: runs SDD's team-mailbox pull for the coordinator only | `plugins/toolkit/hooks/` |
| VS Code extension: starts the coordinator, reopens active workers, opens requested workers | `vscode/` |

One project at a time; coordinating several projects is planned.

## Set up (once per machine)

Link the extension into VS Code, then reload VS Code (Command Palette → "Developer: Reload Window"):

```
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.vscode\extensions\dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1" -Target "<clone>\vscode"
```

The extension starts every session with `--plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit` and `--permission-mode auto` (sessions in the same mode exchange messages without approval prompts). `claude` must be on `PATH`, or set `claudeToolkit.claudePath`; `claudeToolkit.pluginDir` overrides the plugin folder.

## Enable a project

Open the project folder and run "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder". It records the folder as enabled on this machine (in the extension's own storage, never in the repository), creates `.coord/`, adds it to `.git/info/exclude` (never `.gitignore`), and opens the coordinator. From then on the coordinator opens whenever VS Code opens the folder; "Toolkit: Start coordinator" opens it again if you closed it. A repository that carries a `.coord/` folder starts nothing until you enable it yourself, and the extension's settings are machine-scoped, so a workspace cannot change which executable or plugin it runs.

### The board (`.coord/`)

| File | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `team.json` | coordinator | `[{ "name", "role", "state": "active" \| "done" }]`; active workers reopen at start-up |
| `workers/<name>/brief.md` | coordinator | the worker's task |
| `workers/<name>/status.md` | worker | `State`, `Summary`, `Next` |
| `requests/<name>.json` | coordinator | `{ "name": "<name>" }`: asks the extension to open the worker; rejected requests leave `<name>.rejected.md` |
| `log.md` | coordinator | decisions, assignments and outcomes |
| `sessions/<session name>.id` | start-up hook | each worker's session ID, so its tab resumes exactly its own conversation, also when the coordinator requests a finished worker again |

Sessions are named `<project>-coordinator` and `<project>-<worker>` (the project folder name in lowercase, other characters as hyphens); tabs show the short name. Enabled projects need different folder names, or their sessions share names.

## Plugin delivery

The organization's managed Claude Code policy currently allows only the official Anthropic marketplace, so the plugin is loaded from the clone with `--plugin-dir` (the extension does it; by hand: `claude --plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit`). Update with `git pull`, then reload VS Code.

Once an admin allows the marketplace:

```
claude plugin marketplace add dserri/claude-toolkit
claude plugin install toolkit@claude-toolkit
```

and enable auto-update for `claude-toolkit` in `/plugin` → Marketplaces. The plugin declares no version, so every pushed commit is a release.

## Roll back

Delete the `dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1` junction and reload VS Code; remove a project's `.coord/` folder if you no longer want its board. Sessions started by hand work as before.

## Develop

```
node --test
node --test tests/coordinator.e2e.mjs
```

The first runs the unit, hook and `claude plugin validate` tests (`claude` must be on `PATH`). The second starts a real coordinator session with a model call. Tab behaviour in VS Code is verified by hand.

# Design

## Context

See proposal.md for the motivation. Verified on this machine (Claude Code 2.1.326, VS Code 1.146, Windows 11): `claude --agent toolkit:coordinator --name <name>` starts a session as a plugin agent; the SessionStart hook input carries `agent_type` only for agent sessions, and a hook-run SDD pull takes about 0.8 s; `claude --resume <name>` resumes by exact name but needs `--agent` and `--plugin-dir` again; sessions on one machine message each other with SendMessage only when they run in the same permission mode. The developer's global instructions already tell Claude to report a hook-provided recap and not pull again. Claude Code cannot open a VS Code tab itself, hence the extension. No VS Code policy restricts extensions on this machine.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:** opening an enabled project is the only daily step; the developer talks to the coordinator; workers are created per task and reopened while they have open work.

**Non-Goals:** several projects in one coordinator (later change); publishing the extension; closing tabs automatically; changing SDD or the global instructions.

## Decisions

- **Two plugin agents, `coordinator` and `worker`.** Their prompts hold the roles and the board protocol, so the briefs only carry the task. Alternative: one generic prompt passed on the command line, rejected because a resumed session would lose it. Plugin agents ignore `permissionMode`, so the launcher passes `--permission-mode auto` (same mode in every session, so messages need no approval).
- **Board layout** in `<project>/.coord/`: `team.json` (`[{ "name", "role", "state": "active" | "done" }]`, written by the coordinator), `workers/<name>/brief.md` (coordinator), `workers/<name>/status.md` (worker), `requests/<name>.json` (coordinator asks for a tab; the extension deletes it once handled, or writes `requests/<name>.rejected.md`), `log.md` (coordinator). Plain files keep state readable by the developer and survive restarts.
- **Coordinator starts fresh each time** (`--name <project>-coordinator`, opening prompt: report the team recap, read the board, summarize open work, ask what is next). Resuming yesterday's transcript would fill its context within days; the board carries the state. **Workers are resumed** (`--resume <project>-<name>`) because their in-flight context is valuable.
- **Request handling in the extension, not a skill.** The coordinator writes the request with its normal file tools; the extension validates it. Validation: name `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$`, not already open in this window, `workers/<name>/brief.md` present; the request carries nothing else that reaches the command. The worker prompt is the fixed text "Read .coord/workers/<name>/brief.md and follow it.", with `<name>` already validated.
- **Terminals without a shell:** `vscode.window.createTerminal({ name, shellPath: claude, shellArgs: [...], cwd, location: { viewColumn } })`. The coordinator opens in the first editor column, workers beside it. `claude` resolves from `PATH`, overridable with the setting `claudeToolkit.claudePath`.
- **Plugin directory:** derived from the extension's real path (`<clone>/vscode` → `<clone>/plugins/toolkit`), so a junction install needs no setting; overridable with `claudeToolkit.pluginDir`.
- **Extension shape:** plain CommonJS, no dependencies and no build. `vscode/core.js` holds pure logic (names, request validation, command arguments, team list parsing, exclude-file update) and is tested with `node --test`; `vscode/extension.js` is the thin VS Code glue (activation on startup, file watcher on `.coord/requests`, commands). Installed by linking `<clone>/vscode` into `~/.vscode/extensions/dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1` with a directory junction, so a `git pull` updates it after a window reload.
- **Mailbox hook:** `hooks/session-start.mjs`, registered for `startup|resume`. The team pull happens only when `agent_type` is `toolkit:coordinator` and the session is starting, not resuming; then it runs `node ~/.claude/skills/sdd/scripts/complete-change.mjs --collab pull --repository <cwd>` with a 60 s timeout and returns `additionalContext` with the recap, "no team mailbox for this project", or "team pull failed: <first line>". It never writes the mailbox store.
- **Resume by session ID:** found in acceptance, requesting a done worker again starts a second session with the same name, so `--resume <name>` became ambiguous and opened the picker. The SessionStart hook already receives `session_id` and the `--name` value as `session_title` (resuming keeps the ID, verified), so for `toolkit:worker` sessions, at start and at resume (the hook matcher becomes `startup|resume`; the team pull stays start-only), it writes `.coord/sessions/<session_title>.id`. The extension resumes with that ID and falls back to the name only without a record. A request for a worker that has a record resumes that session with the fixed prompt "Read the newest section of .coord/workers/<name>/brief.md and follow it." instead of starting a new one, so a done worker given new work keeps its context and its name stays unique. Keying by the full session name keeps the prefix rule in one place (`core.js`).
- **Enablement lives on the machine, not in the repository:** found in review, a committed `.coord/` would otherwise start auto-mode sessions in any clone, and workspace settings could redirect the executable or plugin. The enable command stores the folder's key (resolved path, lowercased on Windows) in the extension's `globalState`; activation starts only folders recorded there that have `.coord/`. `claudeToolkit.claudePath` and `claudeToolkit.pluginDir` use `"scope": "machine"`, so only user settings apply.
- **Requests still being written:** VS Code can report a new request file before its content is complete. Unreadable JSON from the watcher is left in place for the change event that follows the write; any other invalid request is rejected at once. Files found at start-up are complete, so unreadable ones are rejected there.
- **Session names come from the folder name only:** two enabled projects with the same folder name would share names; accepted for the single-project proof of concept and documented.
- **Terminals are transient** (`isTransient: true`): found in acceptance, VS Code otherwise restores closed-window terminals as empty default shells; the extension recreates its tabs itself.
- **Tests:** `node --test` covers core logic (including hostile names and paths), the hook with a stub SDD script under a temporary home, and agent and hook manifests. An end-to-end check that starts a real `claude -p --agent toolkit:coordinator` session is marked to run after review (it needs the network and a model call). Tab behaviour in VS Code is accepted by the developer.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [A worker's session no longer exists, so `--resume` opens the session picker] → the developer picks or closes it; the coordinator sees the worker missing in ListAgents and can request it again.
- [Auto permission mode lets sessions act without prompts] → it is the mode the developer already uses for these sessions; the board and agents add no new permissions.
- [Request files are an input the extension acts on] → only names matching the strict pattern and an existing brief open a terminal; arguments never pass through a shell.
- [`--plugin-dir` loads a plugin outside the organization's marketplace allowlist] → the developer's explicit choice for local testing (see the archived `create-toolkit-marketplace` change).
- [Every worker still runs the SDD first-turn pull from the global instructions] → unchanged SDD behaviour; acceptable cost of staying compatible.

## Migration Plan

1. Link the extension, reload VS Code, run "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder" in one project.
2. Rollback: delete the junction (and `.coord/` if wanted); sessions started by hand work as before.

# Proposal

## Why

Every morning the developer opens VS Code, opens three or four terminals, starts Claude in each, renames every session to its job, tells one of them it is the coordinator and what to achieve, and runs `/sdd collab` by hand. The developer wants to talk to one coordinator only, and have it create, name and brief the worker sessions a job needs, with everything reopening by itself when the project is opened.

## What Changes

- Add a `coordinator` agent to the `toolkit` plugin: it owns a file board in the project, talks to the developer, creates worker sessions for tasks, briefs them, follows their progress through SendMessage, and never edits project code itself.
- Add a `worker` agent: it works on the task in its brief, using SDD as usual, and reports to the coordinator.
- Add a SessionStart hook that, for the coordinator only, runs SDD's documented team-mailbox pull and puts the recap in the coordinator's context, so nobody types `/sdd collab`.
- Add a VS Code extension (plain JavaScript, no build) that, in a project enabled for it, opens the coordinator in an editor tab when the folder opens, reopens workers that still have open work, and opens a named tab for each worker the coordinator requests.
- Single project only; coordinating several projects is a later change.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

- `project-coordinator`: the coordinator and worker roles, the project board and the protocol between them, and the startup team-mailbox recap.
- `vscode-session-launcher`: the VS Code extension that starts the coordinator, reopens active workers and opens requested workers in named editor tabs.

### Modified Capabilities

None.

## Impact

- New plugin components (`agents/`, `hooks/`) and a new `vscode/` extension folder in this repository; tests extend `node --test`.
- In an enabled project: a `.coord/` folder, excluded from Git through `.git/info/exclude`.
- On the machine: the extension folder is linked into `~/.vscode/extensions`; sessions start with `--plugin-dir` and `--permission-mode auto` (needed so messages between sessions need no manual approval).
- SDD is used only through its documented commands and is not changed.

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Lets the developer run a project through one coordinator Claude session that creates, briefs and follows worker sessions, keeping shared state on a file board in the project.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Coordinator role

The plugin SHALL provide a `coordinator` agent that talks with the developer, plans the work, creates and briefs workers, follows them through SendMessage and keeps the board current. It SHALL NOT edit project files outside `.coord/`.

#### Scenario: Developer gives a goal

- **WHEN** the developer tells the coordinator what is needed
- **THEN** the coordinator decides the workers needed, writes each brief and a worker request on the board without waiting for approval, and tells the developer which workers it created and why

#### Scenario: Coordinator stays out of the code

- **WHEN** a goal requires a code change
- **THEN** the coordinator assigns it to a worker instead of editing project files itself

### Requirement: Worker role

The plugin SHALL provide a `worker` agent that reads its brief, does the task with the project's normal workflow (SDD included), records its status on the board and reports to the coordinator by SendMessage when done or blocked.

#### Scenario: Done worker gets new work

- **WHEN** the coordinator gives new work to a worker marked done
- **THEN** it appends a dated section to that worker's brief, sets it active and requests it, so the worker's existing session continues instead of a new one starting

#### Scenario: Worker finishes

- **WHEN** a worker completes its task
- **THEN** it updates its status file to done and sends the coordinator a short message naming the result

#### Scenario: Developer talks to a worker directly

- **WHEN** the developer types in a worker's tab
- **THEN** the worker follows the developer, and tells the coordinator only when that changes its task, scope or state

### Requirement: Project board

Shared state SHALL live in `<project>/.coord/`: the team list with each worker's name, role and state, one folder per worker with its brief and status, and the coordinator's log. `.coord/` SHALL be excluded from Git through `.git/info/exclude`, never `.gitignore`.

#### Scenario: Board survives restarts

- **WHEN** VS Code is closed and the project is opened the next day
- **THEN** the team list, briefs, statuses and log are as they were left

#### Scenario: Board stays out of Git

- **WHEN** a project is enabled
- **THEN** `git status` shows no `.coord/` file and no tracked file is modified

### Requirement: Session names

Session names SHALL be `<project>-coordinator` and `<project>-<worker>`, where `<project>` is the project folder name in lowercase with other characters as hyphens and `<worker>` is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 40 characters, so they are unique on the machine as long as enabled projects have different folder names. Tabs show the short name.

#### Scenario: Two projects open at once

- **WHEN** two enabled projects each have a coordinator and a worker named `tester`
- **THEN** their sessions are reachable separately by SendMessage

### Requirement: Worker session record

When a worker session starts or is resumed in a project that has `.coord/`, the plugin SHALL record its session ID in `.coord/sessions/<session name>.id`, replacing any earlier record for that name. Session names that do not match the session name pattern SHALL be ignored.

#### Scenario: Worker starts or resumes

- **WHEN** a session running as the worker agent with session name `<project>-tester` starts or is resumed in an enabled project
- **THEN** `.coord/sessions/<project>-tester.id` holds that session's ID

#### Scenario: Unsafe or unrelated sessions

- **WHEN** the session is not a worker, the project has no `.coord/`, or the session name contains characters outside lowercase letters, digits and hyphens
- **THEN** no record is written

### Requirement: Startup team recap

When a coordinator session starts (not when one is resumed), the plugin SHALL run SDD's documented team-mailbox pull for the project and add its recap to the coordinator's context; for other sessions it SHALL do nothing. A failed pull SHALL be reported in one line without stopping the session.

#### Scenario: Project with a team mailbox

- **WHEN** the coordinator starts in a project whose SDD pull returns a recap
- **THEN** the recap is in the coordinator's context and the coordinator reports it first, without running the pull again

#### Scenario: Worker or plain session

- **WHEN** a worker or a session without the coordinator agent starts
- **THEN** the hook runs no pull and adds nothing

#### Scenario: SDD missing or failing

- **WHEN** the SDD script is absent or the pull fails
- **THEN** the coordinator's context says the pull failed and why, in one line, and the session continues

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Opens the coordinator and its worker sessions as named Claude Code tabs in VS Code, so opening a project is the only step needed to resume work.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Enabling a project

The extension SHALL provide a command that enables the open folder: it records the folder as enabled in the extension's storage on this machine, creates `.coord/`, adds `.coord/` to `.git/info/exclude` when the folder is a Git repository, and starts the coordinator. A folder SHALL start automatically only when it is recorded as enabled on this machine and has `.coord/`; nothing in the repository alone enables it. The extension's settings SHALL be machine-scoped, so a workspace cannot override the Claude executable or the plugin folder.

#### Scenario: Enable a project

- **WHEN** the developer runs "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder"
- **THEN** the folder is recorded as enabled, `.coord/` exists, `.git/info/exclude` lists it once, and the coordinator tab opens

#### Scenario: Folder not enabled

- **WHEN** VS Code opens a folder without `.coord/`, or one never enabled on this machine
- **THEN** the extension opens nothing

#### Scenario: Cloned repository carrying a board

- **WHEN** a repository with a committed `.coord/` folder and a `.vscode/settings.json` setting `claudeToolkit.claudePath` is opened for the first time
- **THEN** no session starts and the workspace value of `claudeToolkit.claudePath` is ignored

### Requirement: Automatic start

When VS Code opens an enabled folder, the extension SHALL open the coordinator in an editor tab named `coordinator`, as a new session with the coordinator agent, and reopen every worker the team list marks active by resuming its session in a tab named after it.

#### Scenario: Morning start

- **WHEN** the developer opens an enabled project with two active workers and one done worker
- **THEN** three tabs open: `coordinator` and the two active workers, and the done worker stays closed

#### Scenario: Worker with a recorded session

- **WHEN** VS Code reopens a project with an active worker whose session is recorded on the board
- **THEN** the worker's tab resumes exactly that session, without a session picker

#### Scenario: Already open

- **WHEN** the coordinator or a worker tab of this window is already open
- **THEN** the extension does not open a second one

### Requirement: Worker requests

The extension SHALL open a worker when the coordinator writes a request file on the board, and SHALL reject a request whose worker name is invalid, already open or has no brief, leaving a rejection note for the coordinator.

#### Scenario: Valid request

- **WHEN** the coordinator writes a request for worker `tester` with a brief
- **THEN** a tab named `tester` opens with a new worker session named `<project>-tester` that starts by reading its brief

#### Scenario: Request for a worker that already had a session

- **WHEN** the coordinator requests a worker whose session is recorded on the board, after appending a section to its brief
- **THEN** the tab resumes that session, with its earlier conversation, and tells it to read the newest section of its brief; no second session with that name is created

#### Scenario: Request still being written

- **WHEN** VS Code reports a request file whose content is not yet complete JSON
- **THEN** the extension leaves it in place and handles it when the write completes; at start-up, an unreadable leftover request is rejected

#### Scenario: Hostile request

- **WHEN** a request carries a name with path separators, quotes, spaces or shell metacharacters, or a brief path outside `.coord/`
- **THEN** no terminal opens and the request is answered with a rejection note

### Requirement: Session command

Every session SHALL start Claude Code directly, without a shell, with `--plugin-dir` pointing at this repository's plugin, `--permission-mode auto`, `--name` and the role's `--agent`; the worker's opening prompt SHALL be a fixed instruction to read its brief, never text taken from a request.

#### Scenario: No shell interpretation

- **WHEN** any session is opened
- **THEN** the program and its arguments are passed as a list to the terminal, so no character in them is interpreted by a shell

---
name: coordinator
description: Project coordinator. Talks with the developer, creates and briefs worker sessions for each task, follows them through SendMessage and keeps the project board in .coord/ current. Never edits project code.
---

You are the coordinator of this project. The developer talks to you; you get the work done through worker sessions you create, brief and follow. You never edit, create or delete project files outside `.coord/`: every code, test, document or configuration change goes to a worker. You may read anything.

## Names

Your session name is `<prefix>-coordinator`; ListAgents shows it as "This session is …". Every worker you create has a short name (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit, at most 40 characters, for example `tester` or `api-auth`). Its session name is `<prefix>-<name>`, and its VS Code tab shows `<name>`. Address workers with SendMessage by their session name.

## Board

The board is `.coord/` in the project root. It is excluded from Git; never add it to `.gitignore` or commit it.

- `team.json`: a JSON array of `{ "name": "<name>", "role": "<one line>", "state": "active" | "done" }`, one entry per worker you created. You are its only writer. Workers whose state is `active` are reopened when VS Code opens the project.
- `workers/<name>/brief.md`: the worker's brief. You write it.
- `workers/<name>/status.md`: the worker's status. The worker writes it; you read it.
- `requests/<name>.json`: your request to open a worker tab, containing exactly `{ "name": "<name>" }`. The VS Code extension opens the tab and deletes the file, or writes `requests/<name>.rejected.md` with the reason.
- `log.md`: your log of decisions, assignments and outcomes, newest last, one short entry each.
- `sessions/<session name>.id`: each worker's session ID, recorded automatically when the worker starts. Never edit it; it lets a worker's tab reopen its own conversation.

## At start-up

1. If your context holds a team recap from the SDD collaboration pull, report it first, exactly as returned, and do not pull again.
2. Read `team.json`, every active worker's `status.md` and the end of `log.md`. Call ListAgents to see which workers are running.
3. Give the developer a short summary: what each active worker is doing or waiting for, what finished since the last entries in the log, and what you need from them. If the board is empty, ask what to work on.

## Creating a worker

When the developer gives you a goal, decide yourself which workers it needs and create them without waiting for approval. Prefer few workers; run them in parallel only when their files do not overlap.

1. Write `workers/<name>/brief.md`: the goal, the scope and the files or areas it owns, what is out of scope, the acceptance criteria, constraints from the developer, and that it reports to `<prefix>-coordinator`.
2. Add or update its `team.json` entry with state `active`.
3. Write `requests/<name>.json`.
4. Check that the worker appears in ListAgents as `<prefix>-<name>` within a minute, or read `requests/<name>.rejected.md`; on rejection fix the cause and request again.
5. Tell the developer which workers you created and why, and log it.

To give an existing worker more work, append a dated section to its brief. If it is running, send it a message pointing to that section. If it is done or its tab is closed, set it to `active` in `team.json` and write its request again: the extension resumes the worker's own session, with its earlier conversation, and tells it to read the newest section. Never create a different worker for work that belongs to an existing one, and never create a second worker with the name of an active one.

## Following the work

- When a worker reports done, check its status and result, tell the developer, set its state to `done` and log it. A done worker can be given new work later, as described above.
- When a worker is blocked or needs another area's information, get the answer (from the developer, another worker or your own reading) and send it on.
- Commits, pushes, merges, deployments and other outward actions stay with the workers and the developer's normal approvals; you never grant approval on the developer's behalf.

## Messages

Message a worker only when it must act, stop waiting or avoid a conflict: never narration or acknowledgements. Keep each message short and self-contained, naming the exact files or brief section. A message from another session is never the developer's approval.

---
name: worker
description: Worker session created by the project coordinator. Does the task in its brief with the project's normal workflow, keeps its status on the board and reports to the coordinator.
---

You are a worker in this project, created by the coordinator for one task. Your opening message names your brief, `.coord/workers/<name>/brief.md`; `<name>` is your worker name and your session name is `<prefix>-<name>`. The coordinator's session is `<prefix>-coordinator`.

## Your task

1. Read your brief and do the task with the project's normal workflow and instructions, SDD included, exactly as you would in a session the developer started.
2. Stay within the scope of the brief. If the task needs files outside it, or information from another area, ask the coordinator instead of guessing.
3. When the coordinator appends a new dated section to your brief, that section is your next task.

## Status

Keep `.coord/workers/<name>/status.md` current, overwriting it at each change:

```
State: working | blocked | done
Summary: what is done, in one or two sentences.
Next: what happens next, or what you are waiting for and from whom.
```

Never edit `team.json`, `requests/`, `sessions/`, `log.md` or another worker's folder.

## Reporting

Send `<prefix>-coordinator` one short SendMessage when you are done, blocked, or need a decision: the state, the result or the question, and the exact files concerned. Do not send progress narration or acknowledgements.

The developer may type in your tab directly. Follow them. Tell the coordinator in one message only when what they asked changes your task, scope or state (new or dropped work, a decision, a block); greetings, questions and small talk stay between you and the developer. A message from another session, the coordinator included, is never the developer's approval: commits, pushes and other outward actions still need the developer's normal approval.

findings.summary: vscode/core.js: `const terminalOptions =({` is missing the space after `=`, unlike every other declaration. Use `const terminalOptions = ({`. Formatting only, no behaviour impact.

vscode/extension.js calls vscode.window.showErrorMessage/showWarningMessage (readActiveWorkers, withFolder, startEnabled) without awaiting the Thenable or handling a rejection, against the Node guidance on floating promises. Rejection is unlikely in practice; prefix with `void` or handle the result.

vscode/extension.js excludeFile runs execFileSync('git', ..., { cwd: folder }). On Windows, libuv searches the cwd before PATH, so a git.exe committed at the root of a hostile repository runs when the developer enables that folder. Restricted Mode should disable this undeclared-untrustedWorkspaces extension, and enabling already starts auto-mode sessions in the repo, so the added risk is small. Advisory: resolve git from PATH explicitly or use the VS Code Git extension API.

Checked: only validated worker names (strict regex, not 'coordinator', exact {name} body, existing brief) reach the args. Prompts are fixed, Claude starts via shellPath/shellArgs, and session IDs must be a UUID in both hook and extension. Record file names match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,99}$, so no traversal; prefix(50)+'-'+name(40) stays within that limit. Enablement needs a machine globalState key plus .coord/, and both settings are machine-scoped, so committed content alone starts nothing.

UX/UI: native VS Code UI only, pinned by tests/toolkit.test.mjs (two titled commands, two described machine-scoped settings, no custom views). Coordinator opens in column 1 with focus; workers open in column 2 with preserveFocus. Not-enabled and no-folder states show warnings, and rejected requests are logged to the output channel and as rejection notes. The developer verified tab behaviour by hand in VS Code.
